description: This project uses quantum dots as advanced optical sensors within an interactive 3D dashboard. It simulates how these nanoscale particles detect atmospheric gases on distant planets by mapping their size-dependent bandgaps to shifting light frequencies, effectively turning nanoscale physics into a tool for macro-scale space exploration.
summary: Quantum Dots in Projection is an interactive scientific simulator that demonstrates how size-tunable semiconductor nanocrystals can be used as adaptive optical emitters and spectral reference filters for exoplanet atmospheric spectroscopy. By varying a quantum dot core radius, we tune the effective bandgap and match the emission peak to Doppler-shifted molecular absorption lines in a transiting exoplanet atmosphere. The project visualizes a complete 3D optical bench—from stellar light, to collimation, to quantum-dot resonance tuning, to spectral readout—making advanced space instrumentation intuitive, discoverable, and mission-ready for the next generation of orbital observatories.
details:
Quantum Dots in Projection is a 3D-driven educational and engineering visualization platform that models how quantum-confined nanocrystals can enable compact, tunable, space-ready optical sensing. The application presents an interactive optical bench, a core-shell quantum dot lattice, a live spectral analyzer, and a simulated exoplanet atmosphere. Users can tune nanocrystal radius, switch among material systems such as CdSe/ZnS, InP/ZnS, CdTe/ZnS, and CsPbBr3, and explore how the electronic bandgap shifts with radius and dielectric confinement.

The system also animates the spectral overlap between quantum-dot emission and Doppler-shifted atmospheric absorption features such as Fe I, H-beta, Na I D, O2 A-band, and K I. This helps explain how a tunable QD-based optical system could act as a fast, lightweight alternative to heavy fixed filter wheels and rigid dichroic stacks in future space spectroscopy missions.
